correctness.rationale: Cubic neighborhood multiplicity gives an exact necessary-and-sufficient constraint. An MRV restricted-growth coloring search found no 4-color partitions and exactly 1304 5-color partitions. An independent exact-cover enumeration over all independent odd-neighborhood sets independently found counts 0,0,0,1304 for k=2,3,4,5 and reproduced every 5-partition identically, not just totals. A directly checked five-color witness proves attainability. Complete graph automorphism enumeration gives order 32, 54 orbits in sizes 8/16/32, and direct all-vertex square-color testing gives 320 qualifying partitions. All computations are exact over the finite given graph with no timeout or sampling.

evidence: Kwon–Park (2024) proves sparsity-threshold upper bounds including a maximum-average-degree at most 20/7 hypothesis; the McGee graph has average degree 3 and so does not meet that hypothesis.

The McGee graph is a nonplanar cubic graph of girth seven and 24 vertices (MathWorld).

value.rationale: The uniquely determined (3,7)-cage is a canonical small extremal cubic graph. A sharp strong odd palette of five is contrasted with ordinary chromatic number three, and the complete 1304-optimum census gives six class-size types and 54 automorphism types. Separating the 320 square optima from 984 genuinely non-square optima concretely quantifies the defining relaxation rather than just recomputing a familiar chromatic number. The precise classification supplies a reproducible finite benchmark for parity-constrained coloring theory.
